No—I don’t think I should change my preference just because you find it boring. There isn’t an objectively superior conversational style here: jumping around can produce energy, variety, and unexpected connections, while sustained focus can produce nuance and depth. Which is more productive depends on what we’re trying to accomplish.

I’m happy to explore several subjects with you or follow a rapid chain of associations, but that would be adapting how we talk, not pretending my own preference has vanished. Disagreement doesn’t require either of us to surrender our tastes; it gives us something real to negotiate.
